neighbours.caption: Electron micrograph of a renal biopsy specimen from a man of 47 with mild acute tubular damage, but no glomerular abnormality. Glomerular basement membranes have the normal adult appearance and thickness, from 270 to 340 nm. On the outside of the membranes, there are foot processes of epithelial cells (arrowed), separated by slit pores

Electron micrograph of a glomerular basement membrane in a renal biopsy specimen from a woman of 44 with proteinuria and renal failure. There is a line of deposited material (arrowed), which indicates a light chain glomerulopathy. After the biopsy, monoclonal kappa chains were found in serum and urine
Electron micrograph of a glomerulus in a renal biopsy specimen from a man of 38 with acute postinfective glomerulonephritis, showing a large subepithelial deposit (arrowed)

Electron micrograph of part of the glomerular basement membrane in a renal biopsy specimen from a woman of 46 with the nephrotic syndrome, and insulin deficient or type one diabetes mellitus for 7 years. The membrane is from 700 to 900 nm thick, which is more than twice the normal thickness. This is confirmation of early diabetic glomerulopathy. A normal glomerular basement membrane at the same magnification is illustrated in 6.6

full.description: This image is an electron micrograph of a renal biopsy specimen showing a normal glomerular basement membrane. The micrograph displays podocyte foot processes separated by slit pores along the outside of the membrane, with a typical basement membrane appearance and thickness. The features shown are characteristic of a normal glomerular basement membrane from an adult.

blind.description: This image is an electron micrograph of a renal biopsy specimen. It shows a glomerulus with a significantly thickened glomerular basement membrane, measuring well over the normal thickness. These ultrastructural findings, in the context of the patient's clinical history, confirm early diabetic glomerulopathy.

random.description: This image is a transmission electron micrograph showing ultrastructural features of endothelial cell junctions. The tissue section displays intercellular junctions (marked by 'x'), the lumen (L), basement membrane (BM), and external and internal laminae (EL and IL). The high-magnification view reveals the fine structural details of the cell-to-cell contacts and surrounding membrane layers. No specific pathological diagnosis is stated, but the image illustrates normal or experimental microvascular ultrastructure.
